'''''Aechmea blanchetiana''''', also known as '''orangeade bromeliad''', is a common [[Bromeliaceae|bromeliad]] species found in the restingnas vegetation along the [[Atlantic Ocean|Atlantic Coast]] which is part of the Atlantic forest biome in eastern [[Brazil]]. This plant grows from the State of [[Bahia]] south to [[Espírito Santo]].<ref name=i>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=217832 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>Martinelli, G., Magalhães Vieira, C., Gonzalez, M., Leitman, P., Piratininga, A. Ferreira da Costa, A. & Campostrini Forzza, R. (2008). Bromeliaceae da Mata Atlântica Brasileira: lista de espécies, distribuição e conservação. Rodriguésia; Revista do Instituto de Biologia Vegetal, Jardim Botânico e Estaçao Biologica do Itatiaya 59: 209-258.</ref> It is common worldwide in [[Tropics|tropical]] and [[Subtropics|sub-tropical]] regions for its use as an [[ornamental plant]]. 

== Description ==
Orangeade bromeliad usually consists of many thorny, long [[leaves]], which increases its length as the [[plant]] matures, reaching up to 90cm (36 inches). It can grow up to 120cm (4 feet) in height including the stalk. Despite being known for its orange colour, the plant can also be green, crimson, and yellow.<ref>{{Cite web |title=FPS14/FP014: Aechmea blanchetiana Bromeliad |url=https://edis.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/FP014 |access-date=2023-05-27 |website=edis.ifas.ufl.edu |language=en}}</ref>

In its natural habitat, the plant, like other [[Bromeliaceae|bromeliads]], is most often pollinated by [[Hummingbird|hummingbirds]]. However, it can also be pollinated by [[Bee|bees]], [[Bat|bats]], and other pollinators.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kamke |first=Rafael |last2=Schmid |first2=Simone |last3=Zillikens |first3=Anne |last4=Lopes |first4=Benedito Cortês |last5=Steiner |first5=Josefina |date=2011-08-01 |title=The importance of bees as pollinators in the short corolla bromeliad Aechmea caudata in southern Brazil |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0367253011000521 |journal=Flora - Morphology, Distribution, Functional Ecology of Plants |language=en |volume=206 |issue=8 |pages=749–756 |doi=10.1016/j.flora.2010.12.004 |issn=0367-2530|url-access=subscription }}</ref> similar to how other bromeliads reproduce, this plant typically makes [[Offset (botany)|pups]], although it can also breed in a normal way by making [[Seed|seeds]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ltd |first=GardensOnline Pty |title=Aechmea blanchetiana {{!}} GardensOnline |url=https://www.gardensonline.com.au/gardenshed/plantfinder/show_3290.aspx |access-date=2023-05-28 |website=www.gardensonline.com.au}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Aechmea blanchetiana |url=http://www.llifle.com/Encyclopedia/BROMELIADS/Family/Bromeliaceae/25890/Aechmea_blanchetiana |access-date=2023-05-28 |website=www.llifle.com}}</ref> The plant is most often seen being terrestrial, however it can be an [[epiphyte]] as well.<gallery>
